h1: The 8 Best Cordless Grass Shears of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Cordless Grass Shears: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 8 cordless grass shears compared on voltage, battery platform and blade setup, from 7.2V compacts to 20V two-in-one trimmers.
summary: The WORX Cordless Grass Shear & Shrub Trimmer is the pick for most yards: 20V power plus a 4-inch grass blade and an 8-inch bush blade in one tool. If you already own Ryobi batteries, the RYOBI ONE+ 18V shear is the smoothest fit. Own Makita or DeWalt packs? Buy the bare Makita XMU04Z or the DeWalt-compatible trimmer and skip a second battery. For tight borders and small lawns, the 7.2V WORKPRO is the light option.
intro: A grass shear is a small tool that gets judged on a big question: whose battery does it run on? A shear that arrives with its own pack is convenient on day one. A bare tool that takes a battery you already own is cheaper on day one and cheaper again every year after. Most disappointment in this category comes from buying the wrong side of that choice.

We reviewed eight current shears on paper, covering the full voltage spread from 7.2V compacts to 20V platform tools. The ranking weighs battery situation first, then blade setup (grass only or grass plus shrub), then how much tool you carry for the kind of trimming a small yard actually needs.

products.name: WORX Cordless Grass Shear & Shrub Trimmer
products.verdict: 20V power with both a grass blade and a bush blade. The most capable single tool here.
products.description:
WORX gives you a 20V motor and two interchangeable blades: a 4-inch grass shear and an 8-inch bush trimmer. That covers lawn edges, ornamental grasses and light shrub shaping with one tool, which is rare at this size.

It tops the list because it is the only pick that combines the higher 20V class with a true two-in-one blade kit. The Ryobi and Black+Decker shears match its voltage range roughly, but the 8-inch bush blade is what separates it, and the 7.2V models give up real power for the same two-blade promise.

Buy it if you want one trimmer for borders and small hedges. The caveat is bulk: a dual-blade tool is heavier to hold than a dedicated grass shear, so it is less fun for a long edging session.
products.idealFor: Owners who want one tool for lawn edges and small hedges.
products.skipIf: You only trim grass and want the lightest tool possible.

products.name: RYOBI ONE+ 18V Cordless Grass Shear
products.verdict: Ships with a 2.0 Ah battery and charger, and plugs into the wider ONE+ battery family.
products.description:
The Ryobi is an 18V shear sold as a complete kit, with a 2.0 Ah battery and a charger in the box. You can start trimming the day it arrives, and the battery then works across other ONE+ tools.

It sits just below the WORX because it lacks the second blade. Against the bare-tool Makita below it, you pay for a battery you may not need if you already own one, but you gain a charger and a ready-to-run kit if you do not.

This is the easiest recommendation for a first-time cordless buyer who plans to add more Ryobi tools. The caveat is that 2.0 Ah is a modest battery, so long jobs mean waiting on a recharge.
pros: Battery and charger in the box
Ready to use out of the box
products.idealFor: First-time cordless buyers who may add more Ryobi tools.
products.skipIf: You already own Makita or DeWalt batteries.

products.name: BLACK+DECKER 20V MAX* POWERCONNECT 3/8 in. Cordless Shear
products.verdict: A 20V MAX kit on the POWERCONNECT battery system with a 3/8-inch cutting capacity.
products.description:
Black+Decker pairs a 20V MAX motor with a 3/8-inch cutting capacity and its POWERCONNECT battery system. The spec that matters is that cutting capacity: it tells you the shear is meant for grass and thin stems, not woody branches.

It lands third because it is a solid, plain tool without the WORX blade versatility or the Ryobi's clear battery-in-box pitch. It is a better choice than the 7.2V models when your growth is thick, since it carries more voltage.

Best for homeowners already on Black+Decker batteries. The caveat is the same as any proprietary pack: it only pays off if you will use that battery in other tools.
products.skipIf: You need to cut anything woodier than light stems.

products.award: Best Bare Tool for Makita Owners
products.name: Makita XMU04Z 18V LXT Lithium-Ion Cordless Grass Shear
products.verdict: Bare tool on the 18V LXT platform. Ideal if you already own Makita batteries.
products.description:
The XMU04Z is a bare tool, meaning no battery and no charger. It runs on 18V LXT packs, the same platform used across Makita's cordless line, and it comes from the brand itself rather than a third-party adapter.

That makes it fourth: unbeatable for a Makita owner, but the Ryobi and WORX kits are friendlier to a newcomer because they arrive ready to run. Compared with the DeWalt-compatible trimmer below, this is the more established brand option.

Buy it if you have spare LXT batteries. The caveat is blunt: without one, it is a tool-shaped paperweight, and buying a battery and charger first changes the value math.
products.idealFor: Makita owners with spare LXT batteries.
products.skipIf: You have no Makita batteries yet.

products.name: CRAFTSMAN V20 4 In. Cordless Handheld Grass Trimmer
products.verdict: A V20 two-in-one with a 4-inch grass blade and an 8-inch hedge blade, battery included.
products.description:
Craftsman's V20 trimmer mirrors the WORX layout: a 4-inch grass blade, an 8-inch hedge blade, and a battery in the box. It sits on the V20 platform, so the pack is shared with other Craftsman tools.

It ranks below the WORX because the WORX offers a clearer 20V spec and a stronger reputation for its cordless line, while the Craftsman page is vaguer on power. It beats the single-purpose 7.2V models on versatility alone.

A good fit for existing Craftsman V20 owners who want a two-in-one without a separate kit. The caveat is that the listing is light on motor detail, so compare power before buying.
products.idealFor: Craftsman V20 owners who want a two-in-one.
products.skipIf: You want a clearly stated motor spec before paying.

products.name: WORKPRO 7.2V Cordless Grass Shear & Shrubbery Trimmer
products.verdict: The most compact, lightweight tool here. Handles grass and light shrubs without the bulk.
products.description:
WORKPRO drops to 7.2V and a compact body, which makes it the easiest tool in the roundup to steer around flower beds and fence lines. It handles grass and shrub trimming with the same small footprint.

It ranks sixth because voltage is the trade: at 7.2V it will not push through thick growth the way the 18V and 20V shears can. It beats the SnapFresh below mainly on a more complete spec sheet and a slightly more refined pitch.

Best for small lawns and detail trimming where weight matters more than raw power. The caveat is that anything dense will stall it, so keep a bigger tool for heavier work.
products.idealFor: Small lawns and bed edges where weight matters.
products.skipIf: Your yard has dense, overgrown patches.

products.name: SnapFresh Cordless Grass Shear Bush Trimmer
products.verdict: A 7.2V two-in-one handheld with battery and charger included at an easy price.
products.description:
SnapFresh is another 7.2V handheld, packaged as a two-in-one with the battery and charger in the box. It is the lightweight entry that asks the least from your wallet and your wrist.

It lands below the WORKPRO because the WORKPRO is the more detailed compact option, but the SnapFresh counters with an included charger and battery, which matter for someone with no cordless tools at all.

Best for light seasonal trimming on small patches. The caveat is that a 7.2V tool is a lawn-edge tool, not a hedge-shaping tool, so set expectations accordingly.
products.idealFor: Occasional trimmers on small patches with no cordless tools.
products.skipIf: You trim large areas or thick hedges.

products.name: Cordless Hedge Trimmer Compatible with Dewalt 20V
products.verdict: A bare tool built to take DeWalt 20V batteries. Only worth it if you own them.
products.description:
This is an unbranded trimmer designed to accept DeWalt 20V batteries and sold bare, with no battery or charger. It uses a 20V pack you may already have in the garage.

It ranks last because it is the only third-party option on a major brand's battery, and a third-party tool carries more unknowns than the Makita XMU04Z. It is a hedge trimmer by name, so it is the least grass-shear-like pick here.

Only consider it if you own spare DeWalt batteries and want an inexpensive trimmer. The caveat is fit and support: compatibility depends on the maker, not on DeWalt.
pros: Low entry cost for DeWalt owners
products.idealFor: DeWalt owners wanting an inexpensive add-on.
products.skipIf: You do not already own DeWalt 20V batteries.

methodology.title: Battery situation
methodology.description: We separated kits with a battery and charger from bare tools, then weighed each against the buyer who owns a platform and the buyer who does not.

methodology.title: Voltage class
methodology.description: Voltage ranged from 7.2V to 20V in this field. We treated it as a rough proxy for how well a shear copes with thicker stems.

methodology.title: Blade setup
methodology.description: Grass-only shears, two-in-one grass and shrub tools, and a hedge trimmer were scored by how well each blade layout suits small-yard trimming.

methodology.title: Spec transparency
methodology.description: Listings that state cutting capacity, blade lengths and battery size scored higher than those that leave power details out.

methodology.title: Value within the field
methodology.description: Price tier was compared only against the other shears in this guide, never against outside products.

whatMatters.factor: Pick the battery before the tool
whatMatters.detail: Cordless tools in one family share batteries, so the shear is cheap if you already own the pack and costly if you do not. A bare tool and a kit can differ by the price of a battery and charger. Check your garage first, then buy a bare tool or a kit accordingly.

whatMatters.factor: Read voltage as a power tier
whatMatters.detail: Voltage in this guide runs from 7.2V to 20V. Lower voltage means lighter tools but less force through thick growth, and a stall mid-cut is the usual complaint. If your grass is thick or you want to shape small shrubs, stay in the 18V or 20V class.

A grass blade of about 4 inches handles edges and lawns, while an 8-inch bush or hedge blade is for shaping shrubs. Two-in-one models swap between them. Decide whether you actually shape shrubs; if you do not, a grass-only shear is lighter and simpler.

Cutting capacity states how thick a stem the blades can take, such as the 3/8-inch figure on the Black+Decker. Shears are built for grass and thin growth, not woody branches. Read the number on the listing and keep a pruner for anything thicker.

whatMatters.factor: Weigh the tool in your hand
whatMatters.detail: Edging means holding a tool at a low angle for several minutes. Compact 7.2V models are easy on the wrist, while dual-blade 20V tools are heavier. Choose weight over power if your lawn is small and your trimming is occasional.

faq.q: Are cordless grass shears worth it over a string trimmer?
faq.a: For edges, borders and tight spots, yes. A shear is lighter and quieter. A string trimmer still wins on large lawns, so most yards use a shear for detail work only.

faq.q: Do I need a bare tool or a full kit?
faq.a: If you own a compatible battery, the bare Makita XMU04Z or DeWalt-compatible trimmer saves money. If not, a kit such as the RYOBI ONE+ 18V is cheaper than buying battery and charger separately.

The two-in-one tools such as the WORX and the CRAFTSMAN V20 have an 8-inch blade for light shrub shaping. The 3/8-inch capacity on the Black+Decker is a good reminder that none replace a pruner for woody branches.
For soft grass and small tidy-ups, yes. For dense or overgrown patches, a 7.2V tool like the WORKPRO may stall, and an 18V or 20V pick is safer.

faq.q: How do I keep the blades working well?
faq.a: Brush off clippings after each use and keep the blades dry. Wipe residue from the blades before storing and recharge the pack before a long session.

faq.q: Does the DeWalt-compatible trimmer carry a DeWalt warranty?
faq.a: No. It is a third-party tool built to accept DeWalt batteries, so support comes from the maker rather than DeWalt. Check the seller's terms before buying.

finalTake: For most yards, the WORX Cordless Grass Shear & Shrub Trimmer is the right buy: 20V power and two blades in one tool. Own Ryobi packs? The RYOBI ONE+ 18V is the easy fit. Own Makita? The bare XMU04Z saves money. For small lawns and tight borders, the WORKPRO 7.2V keeps weight down.
